_about: Public-source EU-law demo course for the coverage map (pitch plan row 1). Every input here is public: the learning objectives are quoted from the Ocasys 2025/26 course description of Law of the European Union as reproduced in the University of Groningen's public LLB International and European Law programme file 2025/26; the 12-week schedule is a demo schedule assembled from the Treaty text (EUR-Lex) and leading CJEU judgments (curia.europa.eu). It is NOT the course's official week plan and contains no past exams, lecture material or other non-public text. Cards are short statements of well-known public holdings, written for the demo.
sources: https://www.rug.nl/rechten/studiegids/bachelor/international-and-european-law/programme-files/programme-file-llb-international-and-european-law-2025-2026.pdf (Ocasys description 2025/26, Law of the European Union)

brief.textbook: Public sources only: TFEU, TEU, the Charter, CJEU judgments
brief.learning_objectives:
Understand, apply and analyse the fundamental freedoms of the EU internal market, and their relationship to other policy areas in EU law
Understand, apply and analyse EU citizenship
Understand, apply and analyse the basic principles of the Area of Freedom, Security and Justice and its relationship to the EU internal market
Understand, apply and analyse the relationship between the fundamental freedoms and fundamental rights
Understand, apply and analyse EU competition law
Understand, apply and analyse the enforcement of EU substantive law at EU-level and national level, and the basic principles of judicial protection in the EU
brief.notes: Demo course built from public sources only (see docs/demo/eu-public-demo-course.json).

readings: Joined Cases C-267/91 and C-268/91 Keck

weeks.title: Free movement of capital and links to other policy areas
readings: Case C-367/98 Commission v Portugal (golden shares)

weeks.title: EU citizenship
topics: Equal treatment of economically inactive citizens

weeks.title: The Area of Freedom, Security and Justice
readings: Joined Cases C-404/15 and C-659/15 PPU Aranyosi and Caldararu
Joined Cases C-411/10 and C-493/10 N.S.

cards.back: All trading rules enacted by Member States capable of hindering, directly or indirectly, actually or potentially, intra-Community trade are measures having equivalent effect (Case 8/74 Dassonville; Art 34 TFEU).

cards.front: What did Cassis de Dijon add to Art 34 TFEU?
cards.back: Mutual recognition and the mandatory requirements: indistinctly applicable rules can be justified by e.g. consumer protection or fairness of commercial transactions (Case 120/78).

cards.front: Keck: when do selling arrangements fall outside Art 34 TFEU?
cards.back: When they apply to all traders operating in the national territory and affect in the same manner, in law and in fact, domestic and imported products (Joined Cases C-267/91 and C-268/91 Keck).

cards.front: What did Commission v Italy (trailers) add after Keck?
cards.back: A market-access test: a measure that hinders access to the market for imported products is a measure having equivalent effect (Case C-110/05).

cards.front: Lawrie-Blum: who is a worker under Art 45 TFEU?
cards.back: A person who for a certain period performs services for and under the direction of another in return for remuneration (Case 66/85).

cards.front: Bosman: can non-discriminatory rules breach Art 45 TFEU?
cards.back: Yes: transfer rules that directly affect players' access to the employment market of another Member State are an obstacle even if they apply without discrimination (Case C-415/93).

cards.front: The Gebhard test for restrictions on establishment and services
cards.back: National measures liable to hinder the fundamental freedoms must apply in a non-discriminatory manner, be justified by imperative requirements in the general interest, be suitable, and not go beyond what is necessary (Case C-55/94; Arts 49 and 56 TFEU).

cards.front: Grzelczyk: what is the status of Union citizenship?
cards.back: Union citizenship is destined to be the fundamental status of nationals of the Member States; an economically inactive citizen lawfully resident may rely on equal treatment (Case C-184/99; Arts 20-21 TFEU).

cards.front: Ruiz Zambrano: what does Art 20 TFEU protect?
cards.back: Against national measures that deprive Union citizens of the genuine enjoyment of the substance of the rights conferred by their status (Case C-34/09).

cards.front: Aranyosi and Caldararu: when may an EAW be postponed?
cards.back: Where there is a real risk of inhuman or degrading treatment because of detention conditions in the issuing State, assessed in two steps: systemic deficiencies, then a specific risk for the person (Joined Cases C-404/15 and C-659/15 PPU; Framework Decision 2002/584).

cards.front: Schmidberger: can a fundamental right justify a restriction of free movement of goods?
cards.back: Yes: protecting freedom of expression and assembly is a legitimate interest that can justify a restriction, subject to a fair balance (Case C-112/00).

cards.front: Viking: does Art 49 TFEU apply to collective action by trade unions?
cards.back: Yes: collective action that restricts freedom of establishment falls under Art 49 TFEU and must be justified and proportionate (Case C-438/05).

cards.front: Art 101 TFEU: what is a restriction 'by object'?
cards.back: Coordination that by its very nature reveals a sufficient degree of harm to competition; no need to examine effects (Case C-67/13 P Groupement des cartes bancaires, paras 49-50; a concerted practice can be one by object: Case C-8/08 T-Mobile Netherlands).

cards.front: United Brands: what is dominance under Art 102 TFEU?
cards.back: A position of economic strength enabling an undertaking to prevent effective competition by behaving to an appreciable extent independently of competitors, customers and consumers (Case 27/76).

cards.front: CILFIT: when need a court of last instance not refer under Art 267 TFEU?
cards.back: When the question is irrelevant, has already been interpreted by the Court (acte éclairé), or the correct application is so obvious as to leave no reasonable doubt (acte clair) (Case 283/81).

cards.front: Van Gend en Loos: what is direct effect?
cards.back: Provisions of EU law that are clear, precise and unconditional create rights for individuals that national courts must protect (Case 26/62).

cards.front: Francovich: when is a Member State liable for breach of EU law?
cards.back: When the rule confers rights on individuals, the content of those rights can be identified, and there is a causal link between the breach and the damage (Joined Cases C-6/90 and C-9/90).
